title: 2007 HMMT February Geometry Problem 7
statement: Convex quadrilateral \(A B C D\) has sides \(A B=B C=7, C D=5\), and \(A D=3\). Given additionally that \(m \angle A B C=60^{\circ}\), find \(B D\).

solutions.text: 8. Triangle \(A B C\) is equilateral, so \(A C=7\) as well. Now the law of cosines shows that \(m \angle C D A=120^{\circ}\); i.e., \(A B C D\) is cyclic. Ptolemy's theorem now gives \(A C \cdot B D=A B \cdot C D+A D \cdot B C\), or simply \(B D=C D+A D=8\).
